subject: Blended SKU concessioning and channel split for upcoming private offer
messages:
From: Laura Chen <laura.chen@scalewave.com>
To: diego_fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@scalewave.com
Date: Tue, 20 Jul 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: blended SKU + reseller split for upcoming private offer

Diego —

Thanks for taking this. Quick background: ScaleWave is finalizing a private offer for our new analytics product line (forecasted 12–18 month commit). Procurement asked us to see whether Redwood can provide a blended SKU that combines Reserved Node hours (1-year) + metered inference tokens into a single line item on the marketplace PO. Key asks from procurement:

- One consolidated SKU on the PO (so our finance team doesn't need multiple invoice streams)
- Clear channel margin / reseller pass-through (they want to confirm what our partner margin would be)
- A simple uplift/concession structure if commit thresholds are hit

Timeline: procurement needs an initial pricing structure and a draft PO by next week (target 07/27). We attached our draft PO (ScaleWave_Marketplace_PO_Draft_07020.pdf) and a short internal note on target headroom.

Could you share a couple of packaging options (blended list price + suggested reseller margin) and confirm if Redwood can route invoicing through AWS Marketplace or if we should plan to transact via our reseller? Also important: we need to understand whether reserved node hours are eligible for the same private-offer discounts as metered usage.

Thanks — happy to hop on a 30-min call if useful.

Laura Chen
Procurement Lead, ScaleWave

From: diego_fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>

Date: Tue, 20 Jul 2027 12:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: blended SKU + reseller split for upcoming private offer

Laura — thanks for the background and the PO draft. Looping in Camila (partner ops) and Ben (marketplace pricing) to capture the two routing options and the channel split. Initial quick thoughts below; I'll follow up with a short deck (sku-mapping) + numbers.

Proposed approach (high level)

Option A — Single blended SKU (recommended if ScaleWave wants 1 invoice stream)
- Combine 1-year reserved node equivalent + expected monthly metered token consumption into a single annualized list price
- Suggest a baseline reseller margin of 12% for a direct reseller flow (we can increase to 15% on contracted commit tiers)
- Private offer can be created on AWS/GCP marketplace with the blended SKU; billing can still separate at redemption time for internal accounting but the PO lists a single line item

Option B — Dual-line private offer (conservative)
- Reserved capacity as one SKU, metered inference as another; discounts applied separately per SKU
- Reseller margin: reserved node 10%, metered 13% (example)
- Simpler from a compliance/invoice reconciliation perspective but multiple invoice streams unless routed through a reseller aggregator

Open items we need from ScaleWave
- Target committed $ for year 1 (so we can anchor list prices)
- Preferred invoice path: AWS PO vs reseller-managed invoicing
- Any tax/VAT considerations for your regions of use

Attachments I'm sending: scalewave-sku-mapping-07021.xlsx (mapping of how we'd construct the blended SKU and pricing examples).

If helpful I can draft a quick mutual action plan for procurement to show milestones: pricing approval -> legal redline -> private-offer creation -> DocuSign.

Diego Fernandez
Account Exec, Redwood Inference

Short note on billing mechanics from Marketplace ops perspective:

- If ScaleWave wants a single PO line as per Option A, we need to create a composite SKU (internal mapping) and register it in Marketplace as a single product offering. AWS will still track metered usage events separately on the backend, but docs/invoicing will show one line if we configure the private offer that way.
- If the private offer is transacted directly via AWS Marketplace (vs reseller doing pass-through), we can keep the reseller margin embedded in the list price and pay out to the reseller on a settlement schedule. That keeps ScaleWave's accounting simpler.
- Important: reseller-managed invoicing (where a named reseller issues invoices to ScaleWave) requires a pass-through fee and an explicit distributor/reseller contract. That path can add 30–45 days to onboarding.

Two asks for procurement team:
1) Confirm preferred transaction path (AWS marketplace private offer vs named reseller invoicing).
2) If using a reseller, share reseller legal name and tax ID for routing.

I'll coordinate with Mike on any specific AWS PO constraints (metering + reserved-capacity combined SKUs).

Ben Carter
Head of Marketplace Partnerships, Redwood Inference

Laura — thanks for the patience. Quick summary and ask from Redwood's side after internal alignment:

What we can offer (agreed path)
- Create a composite (blended) SKU for the private offer that lists as one line on the PO.
- Baseline blended list price (example for modeling): $1,200,000 annualized for committed 12-month package (includes 6,000 reserved node hours + estimated 1.2B inference tokens).
- Reseller margin: 12% embedded in the list price. If ScaleWave confirms a $1.5M commit, we can move to a 15% reseller margin on the same SKU (contracted uplift).
- Early-exit / overage handling: metered usage above forecast billed monthly at 78% of public metered rate; reserved hours pro-rated.

Action items for ScaleWave (please confirm so we can finalize the draft PO):
1) Confirm preferred invoice path: (A) AWS private offer (Redwood invoices via AWS settlement) or (B) Named reseller invoicing (require reseller details + tax id).
2) Confirm target commit for year-1 (anchor number for final list price).
3) Legal point: consent to embedded reseller margin (we will include line-item note in the private-offer terms).

Next steps:
- Once ScaleWave confirms items 1–3, Redwood will:
  a) Finalize composite SKU mapping (will upload to Marketplace).
  b) Produce a DocuSign-ready private offer and attach the final PO draft.
  c) Share a short mutual action plan with dates for procurement/legal.

I've prepared the updated pricing table and included a DocuSign link to the draft (https://www.docusign.com/--/envelope/ABC123456789). Diego — can you approve the blended-list price and margin so I can send the DocuSign to ScaleWave?

Best,

Camila Reyes
Partner Ops, Redwood Inference
